## What you need

- **Must (headline):** Python (production), ML fundamentals, Risk & compliance docs (Annex IV, model cards).
- **Important (headline):** Guardrails, LLM evaluation (golden sets, calibrated judges, CI gates), EU AI Act / NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001, Fairness & explainability tools, Observability (OpenTelemetry traces, metrics).
- **Full inventory:** 56 skills (Must 3 · Important 20 · Should 26 · Optional 7), each with its evidence and posting keywords: [responsible-ai-engineer.md](../../03-skills-and-tech/inventories/responsible-ai-engineer.md).
- **Prerequisites:** MLOps or security engineering background in a regulated firm
- **Credentials (tie-breakers, not skills):** IAPP Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional (AIGP) (Optional: optional governance credential). Whether one is worth it: [credential ROI](../../04-certifications/credential-roi.md).
- What to learn first and what to drop across roles: [skills radar](../../03-skills-and-tech/skills-radar.md); in what order: [learning roadmaps](../../03-skills-and-tech/learning-roadmaps.md).

## How to prove it

- **What the evidence asks for:** A compliance packet mapped to NIST AI 600-1 and the OWASP LLM Top 10, with runtime guardrails, subgroup evals and a calibrated judge on ~100 traces
- **Project archetypes that cover the most of its Must and Important skills** (Grade M): [P20 Responsible-AI compliance packet with runtime guardrails](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p20) (100%); [P8 Paper re-implementation with rigorous evals and a write-up](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p8) (42%); [P4 Prompt vs RAG vs fine-tune comparison](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p4) (42%). One project rarely covers a role; the [job-search strategy](../../06-job-search/job-search-strategy.md#the-constraints-that-bind-first) computes the smallest sets that do.
- How verifiable the proof must be, and what to publish: [proof-of-work standards](../../05-portfolio/proof-of-work-standards.md).

## How you are interviewed

- **Track: Governance.** It tests a scoping or solutions round, and fluency in the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001. Source: T1-03, T0-14 (first collected in the role catalog §8.2; this file is the owner).
- **Practise:** the [governance prep pack](../../08-interviewing/prep-packs.md#governance-pack), plus the behavioural and coding packs.
- Classify the loop first, then prepare by round: [interview loops](../../08-interviewing/interview-loops.md).

## Résumé

- **Variant:** E2 Governance & assurance (AI Product, Governance & Assurance); headline pattern: "AI Governance Lead: EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001". How to tailor it: [résumé strategy](../../06-job-search/resume-strategy.md).
- **Keywords to mirror, only when true:** responsible AI, AI governance, guardrails, fairness, explainability, EU AI Act, model cards
- **Leave out or reframe:** Pre-1.0 tools (Guardrails AI, Giskard v3, c2pa-python) presented as production-hardened
